column2: At night one learns news of oneself and of others; "Protect in every fort, Durga" — having worshipped Durga one becomes a slayer of foes.
Having repeated "Ha Sa Ksha Ma La Va Ra Yum," one should destroy the enemy through Bhairavi.
With the sun, gods, fortnights and mountains, a woman is subdued by anointing; with moon, Indra, serpents and Rudras, women are subdued by anointing the yoni.
With lunar days, directions, ages and arrows the pill is subduing; in food, meals and drink the subduing pill is to be given.
With priests, planets, eyes and mountains, worn in the mouth, it paralyzes weapons; with mountains, Indra, Vedas and openings, from anointing the body one may dwell in water.
With arrows, eyes, Manus and Rudras the pill removes hunger, thirst and the like; with three-sixteen, directions and arrows, by anointing an unfortunate woman becomes fortunate.
With gods, eyes, directions and eyes, by anointing one sports with serpents; with gods, eyes, lords and serpents, by anointing a woman gives birth easily.
With seven, directions, sages and openings, by anointing gambling... tongue-weapon; with gods, eyes, oceans and sages, by anointing the banner a son in union.
With planets, oceans, snakes and gods the pill becomes subduing. The power of the herb standing at the priest's station has been presented.
In order the great herbs named one and so on; they are removers of all diseases and make one deathless;
breakers of wrinkles and grey hair, going into all bowels. Their powder, and pills prepared with juice,
a lick or a decoction, a sweet ball, a piece of jaggery, with honey or ghee, or ghee or oil,
taken by oneself in every way becomes revival of the dead: half a karsha or one karsha, half a pala or one pala;
devoted to conduct as desired, one may live three hundred years; in the rule of Mrita-sanjivani there is no better yoga than this.
By the first group of nine one is freed from all diseases; by the second and third and fourth one is freed of ailments;
thus from the sixfold, first, second and third, fourth, fifth, sixth, and likewise from nine and four;
from wind by one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight; from bile by fire, sun, twenty-six and twenty-seven;
from phlegm by arrows, seasons, mountains, Vasus and lunar days one is freed; by Vedas, fires, arrow-qualities and six qualities one holds it in control.
From planets and the rest up to seizure one is freed of all; by one, two, three, flavors, mountains, Vasus, planets, Shiva in order,
by thirty-two, lunar days and suns — no inquiry is needed here. The knowledge of thirty-six words is not to be given to just anyone.
The first, second, eighth and twelfth, a foot-vision — one should leave it. The lord of the day takes a watch; the rest share half-watches;
one should leave Saturn's portion in battle; I tell you day-Rahu: in the east on Sunday; in the northwest on Saturday; Jupiter in the south; Venus in fire;
Mars in fire; on Monday in the north; Rahu is always on Mercury. Phani-Rahu is one watch in the northeast, fire and southwest;
having surrounded the enemy in the northwest he kills one facing the northeast. I shall tell the lunar-day Rahu: in the full moon in the southeast,
on the new moon in the northwest, Rahu, killer of the enemy in front. Ka and the rest, those ending in Ja, are in front; Sa and the rest, those ending in Da, in the south;
one should leave the Mars-groups in the A-less; Dha and the rest ending in Ma in the east; Ya and the rest ending in Ha in the north; one should avoid the lunar-day sight.
Three lines, eastern and southern, in the Mula-breaker; having written the sun's sign and the rest, loss in sight, otherwise victory.
I shall tell the Vishti-Rahu: one should draw eight lines. From Shiva to Yama, from Yama to Vayu, from Vayu to Indra, then Varuna;
from Nirriti one should lead to the moon, from the moon to fire, then to water; from water to Ishana, Rahu of great strength moves with Vishti.
In the northeast from the third, in the south from the seventh; thus in the dark and bright fortnight, in the northwest, Rahu kills the foes.
Indra and the rest, Bhairava and the rest, Brahmani and the rest, planets and the rest; eight and eight in the east and the rest, in the south and the rest the wind-yogini;
whichever direction the wind blows, standing there one should slay the enemies. I shall tell the strengthening: worn at the neck, arms and the rest,
the one uprooted in Pushya wards off an arrow aimed — shara-pungkhika; likewise aparajita and patha: with the two one wards off a sword.

Om, homage to the revered Vajrashrinkhala, kill, kill; Om eat, eat; Om devour; ah, drink blood with a skull, red-eyed, red-clothed, ash-limbed, ash-smeared, vajra-armed, formed of vajra-shape, bind the east direction, bind; Om bind the south, bind; Om bind the west, bind; bind the north, bind; bind Nagas, bind; bind Naga women, bind; Om bind Asuras; Om bind Yakshas, Rakshasas, Pishachas; Om protect from whatever troubles from ghosts, spirits, Gandharvas and the rest; Om protect above, protect below; Om bind the dagger; Om blaze, great-strong, shake, shake; Om twist, twist, with a wall of mane, vajra and fire, hum phat Hrim Hrum Shrim phat Hrim Hah Phum Phem Phah — from all seizers, all diseases, all evil troubles, Hrim, protect from all, protect. One should apply it in seizers, fevers and so on, spirits and all works.
Haum Sphem Ha Sa Kha Ka Chha Da — the Om-syllable is Bhairava, the crest. Bhelakhi the armor; the messenger; the eye-called Raktachandika;
then one should worship the secret Kunjika weapon in the mandala-place: in fire the Kurcha-head, in Rudra's, in the southwest the crest in the wind;
the armor in the middle, the eye, the weapon in the directions in the mandala; in the pericarp with thirty-two the self-mantra seed "Srom Ha Sa Ksha Ma La Na Va Va Sha Da Sa..."
Brahmani, Maheshi, Kaumari, Vaishnavi, Varahi, Mahendri, Chamunda, Chandika from Indra's,
one should worship... in Shiva's, moon's, fire's, Yama's quarters; in the water the five garlands of Matrikas,
Jalandhara, Purnagiri, Kamarupa in order; in Marut, Isha, fire, southwest, in the middle Vajrakubjika;
Anadi-vimala is to be worshipped, praised by Sarvajna-vimala; then Prasiddha-vimala, praised by Samyoga-vimala,
then Samaya-vimala — these five Vimalas; in the northwest, northeast, southwest, fire, and on the northern peak;
for Kubja, Khinkhini the sixth, Sopanna, Susthira, and Ratnasundari in Ishana; on the peak the eight lords;
Mitra, Odisha, Shashthya, Varsha in fire, water, wind; there is Gaganaratna; in the west Kavacharatna;
Brum — a mortal, called the five names, in the wind, Ishana, fire; the five jewels in south and southeast: Jyeshtha, Raudri and Antika;
these three of them are the great old ones; all with five Oms; by difference of twenty-seven and twenty-eight the worship is twofold:
Om Aim Gum — one should worship Kramaganapati, Om, Vatuka; in a square mandala on the right Ganapa one should worship,
on the left Vatuka, in the corner the teachers, sixteen lords; in the northwest and the rest eighteen, at each hexagon corner then;
eight Brahmas around, in the middle nine-natured; Kubjika and Kulata — the order of worship always.
Atala-devi, Shrichandra, up to Devi — these then; one should worship the sandals of Bhagatma-pungana-deva-mohini;
one should worship the sandals rich in the jewel of bliss of the past worlds; Brahmajnana, Kamala, with Parama Vidya;
Vidyadevi, Guru-shuddhi — I shall tell you the threefold purity: Gagana, Chatuli, Atma, Padmananda, Mani, Kala,
Kamala, Manikyakantha, Gagana, then Kumuda; Shri-Padma, Bhairavananda, Deva Kamala;
Shiva, Bhava, Krishna, and the sixteen Siddhas; Chandrapura, Gulma, Shubha, Kama, Atimuktaka,
Kantha, Vira, Prayoga, Kushala, Devabhogaka, Vishvadeva, Khadgadeva, Rudra, and Dhata,
Mudraspheti, Vamshapura, Bhoja — sixteen Siddhas. The body of the Samaya is controlled by the sixfold placement;
having cast a flower on the mandala one should then worship the mandalas: Ananta and Mahanta, and always Shiva's sandals;
Mahavyapti, Shunya, the mandala of the five principles; one should worship the sandals of Shrikantha-natha; Shankara and Anantaka;
Sadashiva and Pingala, and Bhriguananda the lord; Langulananda and Samvarta one should worship in the mandala place;
in the southwest Shri-Mahakala and Pinaki and Mahendraka; Khadga, Bhujanga, Bana, Aghasi, Shabdaka, Vasha;

Ajnarupa, Nandarupa — having given the offering one should worship in order. "Hrim Kham Kham Hum Saum, to Vatuka" — then one should worship the remainder of the offering; "Hrim Hrum Ham Shrim" — the Trikuta.
On the left and right in front, on the south, the sandals of Nishanatha; on the right of Tamorinatha, in front of Kalanala;
Uddiyana, Jalandhara, Purna and Kamarupa; Gagananandadeva and Svargananda with the group;
Paramanandadeva and the sandals of Satyananda; Nagananda, Vargakhya; at the end of the declared, the five jewels;
in the north in Shiva one should worship six, the sandals of Suranatha; one should worship Shrimat-Samayakotisha, Vidyakotishvara;
Kotisha, Bindukotisha, Siddhakotishvara likewise; the four Siddhas in the southeast, one should worship Amarishesvara;
Chakrishanatha, Kurangesha, Vritresha, Chandranatha; one should worship these with scent and the rest; in the south the five Vimalas;
one should worship Anadivimala, then Sarvajnavimala; one should worship Yogishavimala, called Siddha, called Samaya;
in the southwest one should conquer the four gods, Kandarpanatha; the earlier Shaktis and all, one should worship the sandals of Kubjika;
with the nine-fold mantra or with the five Oms; one should always worship the thousand-eyed, blameless Vishnu and Shiva.
From the east to the end of Shiva: Brahma and the rest; Brahmani and Maheshvari, Kaumari, Vaishnavi, Varahi, Shakra's Shakti,
Chamunda and Mahalakshmi — one should worship from east to northeast; Dakini and Rakini are to be worshipped, Lakini and Kakini likewise,
Shakini and Yakini are to be worshipped in the northwest and the six fierce; then having meditated one should worship the goddess of thirty-two letters,
with five Oms or with "Hrim": dark as a blue lotus petal, six-faced, of six kinds,
the power of consciousness, called of eighteen, with twelve arms, seated at ease on a lion-throne, standing above a corpse-lotus,
rich in a thousand crores of clans, Karkota on her girdle, Takshaka above, Vasuki as the necklace;
Kulika at her ears, a tortoise her earring-circle; on her brows Padma and Mahapadma; on the left a Naga, a skull;
rosary, skull-staff, conch and book on the right; trident, mirror, sword, jewel-garland, goad and bow;
the goddess's upward face is white, another upward white; the eastern one pale, the angry south one dark;
the gentle one like snow, jasmine and moon; Brahma stands at the soles, Vishnu at the hips, Rudra at the heart, Ishvara at the throat,
Sadashiva on the forehead; above him Shiva stands. Kubjika, reeling, is to be meditated in worship and rites.
Bha Bhishani on the right shoulder; "Ma" Vayuvega on the left; "Da"-named on the right arm; "Dha" Vinayaka on the left;
Pa Purnima in the two hands; the vowel "O" and the rest on the fingers; "Am" Darshani on the left finger; "Ah" Sanjivani in the hand;
Ta Kapalini on the skull; "Ta" Dipani on the skull-staff; "Ja" Jayanti on the trident; "Ya" Vriddhi Sadhani is remembered;
Sha Paramakhya on the life; "Ha" Ambika on the breath is remembered; "Chha" Sharira on the right breast; on the left Putana on the breast;
A Stanakshira; "Aa" Mota; "Tha" Lambodari on the belly; "Ksha" Samharika at the navel; Mahakali at the hips;
Sa Kusumamala on the secret place; "Sha" Shukradevika in the seed; "Ta" Tara-asya on the two thighs; "Jna" on the right knee;
on the left Kriyashakti; Gayatri on the shank; "O" Savitri on the left shank; "Do" Dohani on the right foot;
Pha Phetkari on the left foot; the nine-natured Malini Manu; "A" Shrikantha on the crest; "Aa" Anantaka on the face;
I Sukshma on the right eye; "Ii" Trimurti on the left; "U" Amaresha on the right ear; "Uu" Arghamshaka on the other ear.
